q.en: What if both training classes have equal counts?
q.zh: 如果两个训练类别计数相同呢？

a.en: Choose and document a deterministic tie rule. The example chooses the smaller class ID. Do not inspect test labels to break the tie.
a.zh: 选择并记录确定性的平局规则。本例选择较小类别编号。不要查看测试标签来打破平局。

q.en: Is a high score on repeated rows automatically fraudulent?
q.zh: 重复测量数据上的高分一定是假的吗？

a.en: No. It may answer a legitimate familiar-group task. The issue is claiming new-group generalization from an evaluation that did not hold groups out.
a.zh: 不一定。它可能回答了合理的熟悉组任务。问题是把未留出完整组的评估，解释成对新组的泛化能力。

q.en: Why not replace every gap with zero?
q.zh: 为什么不把所有缺失都替换为零？

a.en: Zero may be a real measured value with a very different meaning. A gap says we do not know. Choose a rule that matches the feature.
a.zh: 零可能是真实测量值，含义完全不同。缺口意味着不知道。应按特征含义选择规则。

q.en: What does the missing flag [0,1,0,0] preserve?
q.zh: 缺失标记 [0,1,0,0] 保留了什么？

a.en: It records that the second value was unknown before filling. The filled value 4 alone cannot tell us that.
a.zh: 它记录第二个值填补前是未知的。单看填补值 4 无法判断这一点。

q.en: Can we learn the median from test rows?
q.zh: 能用测试行学习中位数吗？

a.en: No. That lets held-out data influence preparation. Fit on training rows and apply the saved rule everywhere else.
a.zh: 不能。这会让留出数据影响准备过程。应在训练行拟合，再将保存的规则用于其他数据。

q.en: Why can 1, 2, 3 mislead a distance model?
q.zh: 为什么 1、2、3 会误导距离模型？

a.en: Those numbers imply order and spacing. Unordered names do not justify that geometry. One-hot columns remove that particular assumption.
a.zh: 这些数值暗含顺序与间距，无序名称并不支持这种几何关系。独热列消除这一特定假设。

q.en: Why save column order?
q.zh: 为什么保存列顺序？

a.en: A learned weight is tied to a column. Swapping paper and wood later changes what that weight means even if the shape stays the same.
a.zh: 学习到的权重对应某一列。以后交换纸与木的列，即使形状不变，也改变了权重含义。

q.en: Is an unknown column a learned solution for every new category?
q.zh: 未知列是否是适用于所有新类别的已学解法？

a.en: No. It identifies the situation. A useful response still needs evidence, a fallback rule, or later labeled examples.
a.zh: 不是。它只是标明情况。有效应对仍需证据、后备规则或后续带标签样本。

q.en: Why square the errors before adding?
q.zh: 为什么先平方再相加？

a.en: Errors +1 and −1 would cancel in a plain sum. Their squares add to 2. Squaring also makes an error of 4 count sixteen times as much as an error of 1.
a.zh: 直接求和时，+1 与 −1 会抵消。平方和为 2。误差为 4 的平方是 16，其影响是误差为 1 的十六倍。

q.en: Does a lower training MSE prove a better future prediction?
q.zh: 训练 MSE 更低是否证明未来预测更好？

a.en: No. Training rows helped choose the rule. Compare models on the same held-out rows to test whether the improvement transfers.
a.zh: 不证明。训练行参与了规则选择。要在相同留出行上比较，才能检查改进能否迁移。

q.en: Why does a negative gradient increase a weight?
q.zh: 负梯度为什么让权重增加？

a.en: The update subtracts learning rate times gradient. Subtracting a negative number adds a positive amount. This moves toward lower loss locally.
a.zh: 更新要减去学习率乘梯度。减去负数等于增加正数，从局部方向看是朝较低损失移动。

q.en: What if the learning rate is much larger?
q.zh: 学习率很大时会怎样？

a.en: A large step may cross the low point and raise the loss. Compare the loss before and after a step; do not assume every descent update succeeds.
a.zh: 大步可能越过低点，使损失上升。要比较更新前后的损失，不能假定每一步都成功。

q.en: Is 0.5987 already a class label?
q.zh: 0.5987 已经是类别标签吗？

a.en: No. It is a probability estimate. Comparing it with 0.50 gives class one; comparing it with 0.65 gives class zero.
a.zh: 不是，它是概率估计。与 0.50 比较得到类别一，与 0.65 比较得到类别零。

q.en: Why is sigmoid(0) equal to 0.5?
q.zh: 为什么 sigmoid(0) 等于 0.5？

a.en: exp(0) equals 1. The denominator is 1+1=2, so the result is 1/2.
a.zh: exp(0) 等于 1。分母为 1+1=2，所以结果为 1/2。

q.en: Does a higher threshold improve every metric?
q.zh: 提高阈值会改善所有指标吗？

a.en: No. It produces fewer positives. Some false alarms may disappear, but some true positives may be missed too. Count both types on validation data.
a.zh: 不会。正类预测会减少，部分误报可能消失，也可能漏掉部分真正例。要在验证数据上同时统计两种变化。

q.en: Why not choose the threshold on the final test set?
q.zh: 为什么不在最终测试集上选阈值？

a.en: Then the reported test score would also reflect a choice optimized on those same outcomes. Keep an untouched final evaluation after the choice is fixed.
a.zh: 这样报告的测试分数也包含了针对同一批结果优化的选择。应先固定阈值，再做未参与选择的最终评估。

q.en: Why can 90% accuracy be useless for finding calls?
q.zh: 为什么 90% 准确率可能无法帮助寻找鸟叫？

a.en: Ninety clips are background. Rejecting every clip gets those ninety right but misses every call. Recall is zero.
a.zh: 九十段是背景。拒绝全部片段能判对这九十段，却漏掉所有鸟叫，召回率为零。

q.en: Why are the precision and recall denominators different?
q.zh: 为什么精确率和召回率的分母不同？

a.en: Precision asks about the 20 flagged clips: 8/20. Recall asks about the 10 real calls: 8/10. Both use the same eight correct detections.
a.zh: 精确率检查二十段标记片段，即 8/20。召回率检查十段真实鸟叫，即 8/10。两者都使用八次正确检出。

q.en: What if no clip is predicted positive?
q.zh: 如果没有片段被预测为正类呢？

a.en: Precision becomes 0/0 and is mathematically undefined. Some software reports zero by convention. State that convention and keep the counts visible.
a.zh: 精确率变成 0/0，数学上未定义。某些软件按约定报告零。要说明约定，并保留原始计数。

q.en: Why can we rank squared distances without taking roots?
q.zh: 为什么可以不开平方就排序？

a.en: For nonnegative values, square root preserves order. The smallest square has the smallest root.
a.zh: 对非负值，平方根保持顺序。平方最小，平方根也最小。

q.en: Can three similar trees all make the same error?
q.zh: 三棵相似的树会犯同样的错误吗？

a.en: Yes. Averaging does not remove a misleading pattern that all trees learned. Data quality and independent validation still matter.
a.zh: 会。平均无法消除所有树都学到的误导模式。数据质量与独立验证仍然重要。

q.en: Why does the correction use target minus prediction?
q.zh: 为什么修正使用目标减预测？

a.en: If the prediction is too high, this difference is negative. Adding a negative correction lowers it. The sign matches the repair we need.
a.zh: 预测过高时，该差为负。加上负修正会降低预测，符号与所需修复一致。

q.en: Why not always use η=1?
q.zh: 为什么不总取 η=1？

a.en: It fits this easy example in one step. On noisy data, full corrections can fit incidental patterns too quickly. Select the rate and round count with validation.
a.zh: 这个简单例子会一步拟合好。但噪声数据中，完整修正可能过快拟合偶然模式。应通过验证选择学习率和轮数。

q.en: What does retaining 80% variance mean?
q.zh: 保留 80% 方差意味着什么？

a.en: Horizontal variance is 4 and vertical variance is 1. Keeping the horizontal direction retains 4/(4+1). It does not mean 80% classification accuracy.
a.zh: 水平方差为 4，竖直方差为 1。保留水平方向得到 4/(4+1)。这不代表分类准确率为 80%。

q.en: Why might a small-variance direction still matter?
q.zh: 方差小的方向为什么仍可能重要？

a.en: A rare but useful difference can have little overall spread. PCA has no labels telling it that this difference matters for a later task.
a.zh: 少见但有用的差别，整体离散程度可能很小。PCA 没有标签来告诉它这个差别对后续任务重要。

q.en: Does score 1 mean certain enjoyment?
q.zh: 分数为 1 是否表示肯定喜欢？

a.en: No. It means the represented directions match. The chosen features may omit pacing, difficulty, or the viewer’s current needs.
a.zh: 不是。它只表示当前表示的方向相同。特征可能遗漏节奏、难度或观众当前需求。

q.en: What if the profile is [0,0]?
q.zh: 画像为 [0,0] 时怎么办？

a.en: Division by its zero length is undefined. Ask for interests or use a clearly labeled general fallback instead of fabricating a similarity.
a.zh: 除以零长度未定义。可以收集兴趣，或使用明确标注的通用后备规则，不要编造相似度。

q.en: Why can worse training MSE give a smaller objective?
q.zh: 为什么训练 MSE 更差，目标值反而更小？

a.en: Candidate B trades 0.4 more MSE for 0.8 less penalty. Its total is 1.4+0.1×1=1.5, below A’s 1.9.
a.zh: 候选 B 的 MSE 增加 0.4，但惩罚减少 0.8。总值为 1.4+0.1×1=1.5，低于 A 的 1.9。

q.en: Which numbers should choose the penalty strength?
q.zh: 应该用哪些数值选择惩罚强度？

a.en: Use validation errors, here fold means 1.2 and 1.0. The training objective helps fit weights; it is not an independent measure of future error.
a.zh: 使用验证误差，这里折均值为 1.2 与 1.0。训练目标用于拟合权重，不是未来误差的独立度量。

q.en: Does 0.8 mean a particular message is partly spam?
q.zh: 0.8 是否表示一条消息有部分是垃圾消息？

a.en: No. The label is still zero or one. Probability describes uncertainty. Calibration concerns frequencies across many comparable messages.
a.zh: 不是。标签仍为零或一。概率描述不确定性，校准针对许多相似消息的频率。

q.en: Can monitoring without labels certify accuracy?
q.zh: 没有标签的监测能证明准确率吗？

a.en: No. It can detect schema or input changes. Measuring correctness requires trustworthy outcomes or labels.
a.zh: 不能。它能发现格式或输入变化，但衡量正确性需要可靠结果或标签。

title.en: Build a majority-label baseline
title.zh: 构建多数标签基线

intro.en: Use training labels to choose a rule, then separate test labels to score it.
intro.zh: 用训练标签选规则，再用独立测试标签评分。

questions.code:
from collections import Counter
train_y = [0, 0, 0, 1]
test_y = [0, 1, 1, 0]
counts = Counter(train_y)
baseline = min(counts, key=lambda label: (-counts[label], label))
predictions = [baseline] * len(test_y)
correct = sum(pred == true for pred, true in zip(predictions, test_y))
print('baseline class:', baseline)
print('predictions:', predictions)
print(f'test accuracy: {correct / len(test_y):.2f}')

title.en: Keep complete devices together
title.zh: 把完整设备放在一起

intro.en: Build the 120-row split without a random library call.
intro.zh: 不用随机库调用，构建这个 120 行的划分。

questions.code:
groups = [device for device in range(12) for _ in range(10)]
train = [i for i, device in enumerate(groups) if device < 8]
valid = [i for i, device in enumerate(groups) if 8 <= device < 10]
test = [i for i, device in enumerate(groups) if device >= 10]
train_devices = {groups[i] for i in train}
test_devices = {groups[i] for i in test}
print('rows:', len(train), len(valid), len(test))
print('shared devices:', sorted(train_devices & test_devices))
print('test error:', 2 / len(test))

title.en: Expose leakage with a deliberately simple memorizer
title.zh: 用刻意简单的记忆器暴露泄漏

intro.en: Mina records two readings from each of four devices. She trains on one reading per device and tests on the other. A model that only remembers device IDs scores perfectly. Then she tests on entirely new devices and the score falls to one half. The model did not suddenly get worse. The first split answered whether it could recognise familiar devices, while the second asked about new ones.
intro.zh: 米娜为四台设备各记录两次读数。她每台拿一条训练、另一条测试，只记住设备编号的模型就得到满分。改用完全没见过的设备测试，分数降到一半。模型并不是突然变差了：第一次划分检验的是熟悉设备，第二次问的才是新设备。

questions.code:
rows = [(device, label) for device, label in
        [("A", 0), ("B", 1), ("C", 0), ("D", 1)] for _ in range(2)]

def evaluate(train, test):
    memory = {device: label for device, label in train}
    fallback = int(sum(label for _, label in train) > len(train) / 2)
    predictions = [memory.get(device, fallback) for device, _ in test]
    accuracy = sum(p == label for p, (_, label) in zip(predictions, test)) / len(test)
    overlap = {d for d, _ in train} & {d for d, _ in test}
    return accuracy, sorted(overlap)

row_train, row_test = rows[::2], rows[1::2]
group_train = [row for row in rows if row[0] in {"A", "B"}]
group_test = [row for row in rows if row[0] in {"C", "D"}]
row_score, overlap = evaluate(row_train, row_test)
group_score, clean_overlap = evaluate(group_train, group_test)
assert row_score == 1.0 and group_score == 0.5 and not clean_overlap
print(f"row split: accuracy={row_score:.2f}; shared devices={overlap}")
print(f"group split: accuracy={group_score:.2f}; shared devices={clean_overlap}")
questions.output:
row split: accuracy=1.00; shared devices=['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']
group split: accuracy=0.50; shared devices=[]

en: Construct repeated measurements with a constant label per device. These synthetic rows make the shortcut explicit.
Fit the memory and majority fallback only on training rows. The tie rule chooses label zero.
Compare a row split with a disjoint-device split. Count shared IDs as well as accuracy.
zh: 构造同设备标签固定的重复测量，用人工数据把捷径暴露出来。
只在训练行拟合记忆表和多数类后备规则；平票时选零。
比较按行划分与设备互斥划分，同时报告共享编号和准确率。

title.en: Fit a median, then reuse it
title.zh: 拟合中位数，再重复使用

intro.en: NaN represents unknown numeric entries in this example.
intro.zh: 本例用 NaN 表示未知数值。

questions.code:
import numpy as np
train = np.array([2., np.nan, 6., 4.])
test = np.array([np.nan, 10.])
missing = np.isnan(train)
median = np.median(train[~missing])
filled_train = np.where(missing, median, train)
filled_test = np.where(np.isnan(test), median, test)
print(f'training missing fraction: {missing.mean():.2f}')
print('training flag:', missing.astype(int).tolist())
print('filled training:', filled_train.tolist())
print('filled test:', filled_test.tolist())
questions.output:
training missing fraction: 0.25
training flag: [0, 1, 0, 0]
filled training: [2.0, 4.0, 6.0, 4.0]
filled test: [4.0, 10.0]

title.en: Encode known and unseen categories
title.zh: 编码已知与未见类别

intro.en: An explicit last column records unknown categories.
intro.zh: 明确使用最后一列记录未知类别。

questions.code:
vocabulary = ['paper', 'wood']
def encode(value):
    return [int(value == name) for name in vocabulary] + [int(value not in vocabulary)]
print('columns:', vocabulary + ['unknown'])
for value in ['wood', 'paper', 'metal']:
    row = encode(value)
    print(value, row, 'sum:', sum(row))
questions.output:
columns: ['paper', 'wood', 'unknown']
wood [0, 1, 0] sum: 1
paper [1, 0, 0] sum: 1
metal [0, 0, 1] sum: 1

title.en: Compare a line and a constant
title.zh: 比较直线与常数

intro.en: Use the same three rows for an arithmetic demonstration.

questions.code:
import numpy as np
x = np.array([1., 2., 3.])
y = np.array([3., 5., 8.])
prediction = 1 + 2 * x
residual = prediction - y
mse = np.mean(residual ** 2)
baseline_mse = np.mean((y.mean() - y) ** 2)
print('prediction:', prediction.tolist())
print(f'MSE: {mse:.6f}; RMSE: {np.sqrt(mse):.6f}')
print(f'constant MSE: {baseline_mse:.6f}')

title.en: Standardize and take one step
title.zh: 标准化后更新一步

intro.en: All gradients below use the old parameter values.
intro.zh: 下面所有梯度都使用更新前的参数。

questions.code:
import numpy as np
x = np.array([2., 6.]); y = np.array([1., 3.])
z = (x - x.mean()) / x.std()
w, b, rate = 0., 0., 0.1
error = w * z + b - y
gw = 2 * np.mean(error * z)
gb = 2 * np.mean(error)
w, b = w - rate * gw, b - rate * gb
print('scaled inputs:', z.tolist())
print(f'gradients: {gw:.1f}, {gb:.1f}')
print(f'weights: {w:.1f}, {b:.1f}')
print(f'loss: {np.mean((w * z + b - y) ** 2):.3f}')

title.en: One probability, two decisions
title.zh: 同一个概率，两种决策

intro.en: Use illustrative fixed weights, not a trained sky classifier.
intro.zh: 使用示意性的固定权重，不是真实训练的夜空分类器。

questions.code:
from math import exp
x, w, b = 2., 0.8, -1.2
score = b + w * x
probability = 1 / (1 + exp(-score))
print(f'score: {score:.4f}; probability: {probability:.4f}')
for threshold in [0.50, 0.65]:
    label = int(probability >= threshold)
    print(f'threshold {threshold:.2f}: class {label}')
questions.output:
score: 0.4000; probability: 0.5987
threshold 0.50: class 1
threshold 0.65: class 0

title.en: Choose a decision threshold with an explicit error cost
title.zh: 用明确错误代价选择决策阈值

intro.en: A school machine flags damaged practice parts for inspection. Missing a damaged part costs four effort units; inspecting a good part costs one. Mina first uses the usual 0.5 threshold. She then writes out the two types of mistakes on a small validation set. Lowering the threshold catches a missed damaged part while adding only one unnecessary inspection. She freezes the choice before looking at the final test set.
intro.zh: 学校机器把损坏的练习零件送去检查。漏掉坏件的代价记为四个工作单位，误查好件记为一个。米娜先用常见的 0.5 阈值，再在小验证集上列出两种错误。降低阈值能补获一个坏件，只多一次误查。她在查看最终测试集之前固定阈值。

questions.code:
scores = [0.10, 0.35, 0.45, 0.60, 0.80]
truth = [0, 1, 0, 1, 1]

def cost_at(threshold):
    predicted = [int(score >= threshold) for score in scores]
    fp = sum(p == 1 and y == 0 for p, y in zip(predicted, truth))
    fn = sum(p == 0 and y == 1 for p, y in zip(predicted, truth))
    return fp + 4 * fn, fp, fn

candidates = [0.30, 0.50, 0.70, 1.10]
for threshold in candidates:
    cost, fp, fn = cost_at(threshold)
    print(f"threshold={threshold:.2f} FP={fp} FN={fn} cost={cost}")
best = min(candidates, key=lambda t: (cost_at(t)[0], t))
assert best == 0.30 and cost_at(best) == (1, 1, 0)
print(f"selected on validation: {best:.2f}")
questions.output:
threshold=0.30 FP=1 FN=0 cost=1
threshold=0.50 FP=0 FN=1 cost=4
threshold=0.70 FP=0 FN=2 cost=8
threshold=1.10 FP=0 FN=3 cost=12
selected on validation: 0.30

en: State costs before comparing thresholds. Here the objective is FP+4*FN, not accuracy.
For each candidate, form predictions with score >= threshold and count both error types.
Minimize validation cost and state the tie rule. Keep the final test set separate from this choice.
zh: 比较阈值前先规定代价；本例优化 FP+4×FN，而不是准确率。
每个候选阈值都用 score>=threshold 产生预测，再统计两种错误。
最小化验证代价并说明平局规则；最终测试集不参与选择。

title.en: Compute four metrics from counts
title.zh: 从计数计算四个指标

intro.en: These counts describe one threshold on an invented evaluation set.
intro.zh: 这些计数描述自拟评估集上一个阈值的结果。

questions.code:
tp, tn, fp, fn = 8, 78, 12, 2
total = tp + tn + fp + fn
accuracy = (tp + tn) / total
precision = tp / (tp + fp)
recall = tp / (tp + fn)
f1 = 2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn)
for name, value in [('accuracy', accuracy), ('precision', precision),
                    ('recall', recall), ('F1', f1)]:
    print(f'{name}: {value:.3f}')
print('clips to review:', tp + fp)
questions.output:
accuracy: 0.860
precision: 0.400
recall: 0.800
F1: 0.533
clips to review: 20

title.en: Inspect every nearest-neighbour vote
title.zh: 检查每一张近邻投票

intro.en: The table is synthetic and already uses comparable feature scales.
intro.zh: 表格为合成数据，两个特征已经采用可比尺度。

questions.code:
import numpy as np
x = np.array([[0.,0.], [1.,0.], [2.,0.], [4.,0.]])
y = np.array([0,0,1,1])
query = np.array([1.6,0.])
squared = np.sum((x - query) ** 2, axis=1)
order = np.argsort(squared, kind='stable')
print('squared distances:', np.round(squared, 2).tolist())
for k in [1,3]:
    labels = y[order[:k]]
    print('k:', k, 'labels:', labels.tolist(), 'prediction:', int(labels.mean() > 0.5))

title.en: Majority baseline on a different test mix
title.zh: 测试集比例变化时的多数类基线

prompt.en:
Mia sorts club emails into "event" notices and "other" messages. Her training set has 20 emails: 14 other and 6 event. Her test set has 12 emails: 5 other and 7 event.

Before training any model, she builds the majority-label baseline from the training labels and scores it on the test set. What is its test accuracy? Give a decimal to 3 places.
prompt.zh:
Mia 把社团邮件分成「活动通知」（event）和「其他消息」（other）两类。训练集有 20 封邮件：14 封 other，6 封 event。测试集有 12 封邮件：5 封 other，7 封 event。

在训练任何模型之前，她先用训练标签建立多数类基线，再在测试集上给它打分。这个基线的测试准确率是多少？答案用小数表示，保留 3 位小数。

solution.en:
Step 1: choose the rule from the training labels. other appears 14 times and event 6 times, so c* = other.

Step 2: apply it to every test email. The baseline predicts other for all 12 test emails.

Step 3: count the correct predictions. Only the 5 emails that really are other are correct, so accuracy = 5 / 12 = 0.417.

Meaning: 70% of the training emails were other, but this test set has a different mix, so the baseline is right only 41.7% of the time. Every later model must beat 0.417 on these same 12 emails.

A common slip is to pick the majority from the test labels (event, giving 7 / 12 = 0.583). That uses the test answers to build the rule.
solution.zh:
第 1 步：用训练标签选择规则。other 出现 14 次，event 出现 6 次，所以 c* = other。

第 2 步：把规则用到每一封测试邮件上。基线对全部 12 封测试邮件都预测 other。

第 3 步：数出预测正确的数量。只有真正属于 other 的 5 封是对的，所以准确率 = 5 / 12 = 0.417。

含义：训练集中 70% 的邮件是 other，但测试集的比例不同，所以这个基线只有 41.7% 的时候是对的。之后的每个模型都必须在同样这 12 封邮件上超过 0.417。

常见错误是按测试标签选多数类（选 event，得到 7 / 12 = 0.583）。这等于用测试答案来制定规则。

questions.verify_code:
from collections import Counter
train = ['other'] * 14 + ['event'] * 6
test = ['other'] * 5 + ['event'] * 7
counts = Counter(train)
baseline = max(counts, key=counts.get)
correct = sum(label == baseline for label in test)
print(baseline, correct, len(test))
print(round(correct / len(test), 4))

title.en: Mean baseline for a regression target
title.zh: 回归目标的均值基线

prompt.en:
Leon predicts how many minutes a delivery takes. Before fitting anything, he uses the regression baseline that always predicts the training mean.

Training times (minutes): 12, 15, 18, 15.
Test times (minutes): 14, 20, 11.

What is the baseline's mean squared error (MSE) on the test set, in squared minutes?
prompt.zh:
Leon 要预测一次送货需要多少分钟。在拟合任何模型之前，他先使用回归基线：永远预测训练目标的均值。

训练时间（分钟）：12、15、18、15。
测试时间（分钟）：14、20、11。

这个基线在测试集上的均方误差（MSE）是多少？单位是「分钟的平方」。

solution.en:
Step 1: the training mean is (12 + 15 + 18 + 15) / 4 = 60 / 4 = 15 minutes. The baseline predicts 15 for every test delivery.

Step 2: test errors (prediction minus measurement) are 15 − 14 = 1, 15 − 20 = −5 and 15 − 11 = 4.

Step 3: squared errors are 1, 25 and 16. Their sum is 42.

Step 4: MSE = 42 / 3 = 14 squared minutes. The RMSE is √14 ≈ 3.74 minutes, which is in the same unit as the target.

Two traps: the mean must come from the training times, not the test times (the test mean is 15 here by coincidence, but you may not use it); and the MSE is averaged over the 3 test deliveries, not the 4 training ones.
solution.zh:
第 1 步：训练均值是 (12 + 15 + 18 + 15) / 4 = 60 / 4 = 15 分钟。基线对每一次测试送货都预测 15。

第 2 步：测试误差（预测减实测）分别是 15 − 14 = 1、15 − 20 = −5、15 − 11 = 4。

第 3 步：平方误差是 1、25、16，总和为 42。

第 4 步：MSE = 42 / 3 = 14（分钟的平方）。RMSE 是 √14 ≈ 3.74 分钟，单位与目标相同。

两个陷阱：均值必须来自训练时间，而不是测试时间（这里测试均值碰巧也是 15，但不能拿来用）；MSE 要对 3 次测试送货求平均，而不是对 4 条训练记录求平均。

questions.verify_code:
train = [12, 15, 18, 15]
test = [14, 20, 11]
mean = sum(train) / len(train)
squares = [(mean - y) ** 2 for y in test]
print('mean', mean, 'squares', squares)
print(sum(squares) / len(test))

title.en: A split for machines nobody has seen
title.zh: 面向从未见过的机器的数据划分

prompt.en:
Iris wants to warn before a vending machine fails. Her table has 300 rows: 15 service sessions from each of 20 machines. Columns: temperature, vibration, hours since last service, technician_note (typed by the technician after a failure has been repaired), and the label failed_next_session.

Her question: will the warning work on machines that are installed next year and are not in the table? Which evaluation answers that question?
prompt.zh:
Iris 想在自动售货机出故障之前发出预警。她的表格有 300 行：20 台机器，每台 15 次维护记录。列包括：温度、振动、距上次维护的小时数、technician_note（技术员在故障修好之后填写的说明），以及标签 failed_next_session。

她的问题是：预警对明年才安装、表格里没有的机器是否有效？哪种评估方式能回答这个问题？

text.en: Split by machine: put all sessions of 14 machines in training, 3 in validation and 3 in test, and drop technician_note.
text.zh: 按机器划分：14 台机器的全部记录放进训练集，3 台放进验证集，3 台放进测试集，并删除 technician_note。

why.en: Right. Whole machines are held out, so the test machines are unfamiliar, like next year's machines. The note is written after a failure, so it is not available when the warning must be made.
why.zh: 正确。整台机器被留出，测试机器对模型是陌生的，正像明年的新机器。说明文字是在故障之后才写的，发出预警时还拿不到。

text.en: Random 70/15/15 row split, keeping every column, because random splits are unbiased.
text.zh: 按行随机 70/15/15 划分，保留所有列，因为随机划分是无偏的。

why.en: Wrong. Sessions of the same machine land in both training and test, so the test machines are not new. The note also leaks the answer, because it exists only after a failure.
why.zh: 错误。同一台机器的记录会同时出现在训练集和测试集，测试机器并不是新的。说明文字也会泄漏答案，因为它只在故障之后才存在。

text.en: Split by machine, but keep technician_note because it raises validation accuracy.
text.zh: 按机器划分，但保留 technician_note，因为它能提高验证准确率。

why.en: Wrong. A higher score from a column that is written after the failure is leakage. At prediction time the note does not exist yet.
why.zh: 错误。来自故障后才填写的列的高分就是泄漏。预测的时候这条说明还不存在。

text.en: Time split: the first 10 sessions of every machine for training, the last 5 for testing.
text.zh: 按时间划分：每台机器前 10 次记录用于训练，后 5 次用于测试。

why.en: Wrong for this question. It answers "later sessions on machines we already know". Every test machine was seen in training, so it says little about new machines.
why.zh: 对这个问题来说是错的。它回答的是「已知机器的后续记录」。每台测试机器都在训练中出现过，所以几乎说明不了新机器的情况。

title.en: Find the leaks in a library-loan model
title.zh: 找出图书借阅模型中的泄漏

prompt.en:
Noah wants to predict, on the day an item is borrowed, whether the loan will be returned late. His table has one row per loan from the last three years. Columns:

member_id, item_type, branch, loan_date, member_loans_last_year, days_overdue (filled in when the item comes back), and the label late (1 if returned after the due date).

Many members have dozens of loans. He fills missing values with medians computed over the whole table, makes a random 80/20 row split, and reports accuracy 0.98.

(a) Name two things in this setup that leak information the model would not have on the day of borrowing.
(b) The library will run the model on next month's loans, mostly by the same members. Propose a split that matches this use and say why.
(c) Give two things he should report besides a single accuracy figure.
prompt.zh:
Noah 想在物品被借出的当天预测：这笔借阅会不会逾期归还。他的表格每行是一笔借阅，覆盖过去三年。列包括：

member_id、item_type、branch、loan_date、member_loans_last_year、days_overdue（在物品归还时才填写），以及标签 late（逾期归还记为 1）。

很多读者有几十笔借阅。他用整张表计算的中位数填补缺失值，按行随机做 80/20 划分，并报告准确率 0.98。

(a) 指出这个设置中两处泄漏：模型在借出当天本来不可能拥有的信息。
(b) 图书馆会把模型用在下个月的借阅上，借阅者大多是同一批读者。请提出一种符合这种用途的划分方式，并说明原因。
(c) 除了一个准确率数字之外，他还应该报告哪两样东西？

solution.en:
(a) Leaks.
- days_overdue is filled in only when the item comes back. It almost defines the label (late means days_overdue > 0), so the 0.98 mostly measures this column. Drop it.
- The medians were computed over the whole table, so test rows helped set the training inputs. Fit the fill values on training rows only and reuse them.
- Also check member_loans_last_year: it must count only loans before loan_date. If it was computed over the full history, it uses the future.

(b) Split by time. Train on the oldest loans (for example the first two years), validate on the next few months, and test on the most recent months. Compute every feature and fill value from earlier data only. This copies the real use: the model is trained on the past and predicts the next month. The same members can appear in training and test, because the real use is also mostly known members. If new members matter, report them as a separate group.

(c) Report:
- a baseline on the same test months, such as "never late" (late loans may be rare, so its accuracy can already be high);
- the confusion counts, or precision and recall for the late class, because accuracy alone hides missed late loans;
- the split rule, the prediction time (day of borrowing) and the number of test loans.
solution.zh:
(a) 泄漏。
- days_overdue 只有在物品归还时才填写。它几乎直接定义了标签（逾期就意味着 days_overdue > 0），所以 0.98 主要是在衡量这一列。应删除它。
- 中位数是用整张表算的，测试行参与了训练输入的设定。应只用训练行拟合填补值，再在其他数据上重复使用。
- 还要检查 member_loans_last_year：它只能统计 loan_date 之前的借阅。如果它是用全部历史算的，就用到了未来的信息。

(b) 按时间划分。用最早的借阅训练（例如前两年），用接下来几个月验证，用最近几个月测试。每个特征和填补值都只用更早的数据计算。这样模拟了真实用途：模型用过去训练，预测下个月。同一批读者可以同时出现在训练集和测试集，因为真实用途也主要面对已知读者。如果新读者也很重要，就把他们作为单独的一组报告。

(c) 应报告：
- 在同样测试月份上的基线，例如「永不逾期」（逾期借阅可能很少，所以基线的准确率本身就可能很高）；
- 混淆矩阵的计数，或逾期类的精确率和召回率，因为单看准确率会掩盖漏掉的逾期借阅；
- 划分规则、预测时刻（借出当天）以及测试借阅的数量。

text.en: Names days_overdue as leakage because it is known only after the item is returned.
text.zh: 指出 days_overdue 是泄漏，因为它只有在物品归还后才知道。

text.en: Names a preprocessing or feature leak: medians fitted on the whole table (or counts that include later loans); says to fit on training rows only.
text.zh: 指出预处理或特征泄漏：用整张表拟合中位数（或计数包含了以后的借阅）；说明应只用训练行拟合。

text.en: Proposes a time-ordered train / validation / test split (older loans for training, most recent months for testing).
text.zh: 提出按时间顺序的训练 / 验证 / 测试划分（较早借阅用于训练，最近几个月用于测试）。

text.en: Justifies the split by the real use: predicting next month from the past, with features computed only from earlier data.
text.zh: 用真实用途说明划分的理由：用过去预测下个月，特征只用更早的数据计算。

text.en: Reports a simple baseline (for example "never late") on the same test loans.
text.zh: 在同样的测试借阅上报告一个简单基线（例如「永不逾期」）。

text.en: Reports confusion counts or precision and recall for the late class, not only accuracy.
text.zh: 报告混淆矩阵计数或逾期类的精确率和召回率，而不只是准确率。

mistakes.en: Keeping days_overdue because it is "the most predictive feature".
mistakes.zh: 因为 days_overdue 是「预测力最强的特征」就保留它。

mistakes.en: Proposing only a split by member. That answers a different question (brand-new members), not next month's loans.
mistakes.zh: 只提出按读者分组划分。这回答的是另一个问题（全新的读者），而不是下个月的借阅。

mistakes.en: Recomputing the median separately on the test rows instead of reusing the training median.
mistakes.zh: 在测试行上重新计算中位数，而不是重复使用训练中位数。

title.en: Fill a gap after spotting an error code
title.zh: 识别错误代码后再填补缺口

prompt.en:
Emma's training column of room temperatures (°C) is:
21, 999, 19, missing, 24, 18

The sensor guide says 999 means "read error". Her test column is: missing, 23.

She marks error codes as missing, uses the median of the observed training values as the fill value, and keeps a separate missing flag. What value fills the missing test reading?
prompt.zh:
Emma 的训练列记录了室温（°C）：
21、999、19、缺失、24、18

传感器说明书写明 999 表示「读取错误」。她的测试列是：缺失、23。

她把错误代码标记为缺失，用训练集中观测值的中位数作为填补值，并单独保留一个缺失标记。测试列中缺失的那个读数应填入什么值？

solution.en:
Step 1: mark the error code. The training column becomes 21, missing, 19, missing, 24, 18. Two of six values are missing, so r = 2 / 6 = 0.333.

Step 2: take the observed training values and sort them: 18, 19, 21, 24. There is an even number of values, so the median is the mean of the middle two: (19 + 21) / 2 = 20.

Step 3: fill training as 21, 20, 19, 20, 24, 18 with flags 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0.

Step 4: reuse the same median for the test set. The test column becomes 20, 23 with flags 1, 0. The answer is 20 °C.

Wrong paths and what they give: keeping 999 as a real reading gives the median of 18, 19, 21, 24, 999, which is 21; recomputing a median on the test values gives 23; filling with zero gives 0 °C, a temperature nobody measured.
solution.zh:
第 1 步：标记错误代码。训练列变成 21、缺失、19、缺失、24、18。六个值中有两个缺失，所以 r = 2 / 6 = 0.333。

第 2 步：取出训练集中的观测值并排序：18、19、21、24。值的个数是偶数，所以中位数是中间两个值的平均：(19 + 21) / 2 = 20。

第 3 步：训练列填补为 21、20、19、20、24、18，缺失标记为 0、1、0、1、0、0。

第 4 步：测试集重复使用同一个中位数。测试列变成 20、23，缺失标记为 1、0。答案是 20 °C。

错误做法及其结果：把 999 当作真实读数，中位数变成 18、19、21、24、999 的中位数 21；在测试值上重新算中位数得到 23；用零填补得到 0 °C，这是谁也没有测到的温度。

questions.verify_code:
import numpy as np
train = np.array([21, 999, 19, np.nan, 24, 18], float)
train[train == 999] = np.nan
test = np.array([np.nan, 23.])
flag = np.isnan(train)
median = np.median(train[~flag])
print('missing fraction', round(float(flag.mean()), 4), 'flags', flag.astype(int).tolist())
print('filled test', np.where(np.isnan(test), median, test).tolist())
print(float(median))

title.en: One-hot columns with an unknown slot
title.zh: 带「未知」列的独热编码

prompt.en: Leon builds the vocabulary for a transport-mode column from the training values, then encodes two values. Write the exact output.
prompt.zh: Leon 用训练集中的值为「交通方式」这一列建立词表，然后对两个值进行编码。请写出程序的准确输出。

questions.code:
train = ['tram', 'bus', 'ferry', 'bus', 'tram']
vocab = sorted(set(train))

def encode(value):
    return [int(value == name) for name in vocab] + [int(value not in vocab)]

print(vocab)
for value in ['ferry', 'bike']:
    print(value, encode(value))
print(len(encode('bus')), sum(encode('bike')))

en: set(train) removes the repeats and keeps tram, bus and ferry. sorted puts them in alphabetical order, so the vocabulary and column order is ['bus', 'ferry', 'tram'].
encode('ferry') compares ferry with bus, ferry and tram, giving [0, 1, 0]. ferry is in the vocabulary, so the unknown flag is 0. The row is [0, 1, 0, 0].
encode('bike') matches none of the three names, giving [0, 0, 0], and bike is not in the vocabulary, so the unknown flag is 1: [0, 0, 0, 1].
Every encoded row has 3 + 1 = 4 entries, so len(encode('bus')) is 4. Each row has exactly one 1, so sum(encode('bike')) is 1. The line is 4 1.
zh: set(train) 去掉重复值，只留下 tram、bus、ferry。sorted 按字母顺序排列，所以词表和列顺序是 ['bus', 'ferry', 'tram']。
encode('ferry') 把 ferry 依次与 bus、ferry、tram 比较，得到 [0, 1, 0]。ferry 在词表中，所以未知标记是 0，整行是 [0, 1, 0, 0]。
encode('bike') 与三个名字都不相同，得到 [0, 0, 0]；bike 不在词表中，未知标记为 1，整行是 [0, 0, 0, 1]。
每一行编码都有 3 + 1 = 4 个元素，所以 len(encode('bus')) 是 4。每一行恰好有一个 1，所以 sum(encode('bike')) 是 1。这一行输出 4 1。

title.en: Integer codes for colours
title.zh: 用整数给颜色编码

prompt.en: Leon has a column "bin colour" with the values red, green and blue. He codes them red = 1, green = 2, blue = 3 and feeds the code to a k-nearest-neighbours model. Which statement is correct?
prompt.zh: Leon 有一列「垃圾桶颜色」，取值为 red、green、blue。他把它们编码为 red = 1、green = 2、blue = 3，然后把这个编码交给 k 近邻模型。下列哪项说法正确？

text.en: The codes invent an order and a spacing: blue is now 2 away from red but green is only 1 away. With one-hot columns every pair of different colours is the same distance apart, √2.
text.zh: 这种编码凭空制造了顺序和间距：blue 与 red 相距 2，而 green 只相距 1。改用独热编码后，任意两种不同颜色之间的距离都相同，都是 √2。

why.en: Right. red = [1, 0, 0] and blue = [0, 0, 1] differ in two places, so their squared distance is 2 and their distance is √2, the same as for any other pair.
why.zh: 正确。red = [1, 0, 0] 与 blue = [0, 0, 1] 有两处不同，平方距离为 2，距离为 √2，与其他任何一对颜色相同。

text.en: Integer codes are harmless for k-NN, because it only ranks distances and never uses their size.
text.zh: 整数编码对 k 近邻无害，因为它只对距离排序，从不使用距离的大小。

why.en: Wrong. The ranking is built from those invented distances, so the invented spacing changes which neighbours are chosen.
why.zh: 错误。排序正是由这些凭空制造的距离决定的，所以虚构的间距会改变选出的邻居。

text.en: One-hot encoding adds new rows, one for each colour.
text.zh: 独热编码会增加新的行，每种颜色一行。

why.en: Wrong. It adds columns (one indicator per known colour). The number of examples does not change.
why.zh: 错误。它增加的是列（每种已知颜色一个指示列），样本的行数不变。

text.en: Build the vocabulary from the training and test data together, so that no test colour is ever unknown.
text.zh: 把训练数据和测试数据合在一起建立词表，这样测试中就不会出现未知颜色。

why.en: Wrong. The vocabulary must be fitted on training data only. A colour first seen in testing needs an explicit rule, such as an unknown column.
why.zh: 错误。词表只能用训练数据拟合。测试中第一次出现的颜色需要明确的规则，例如一个未知列。

title.en: One big miss under squared error
title.zh: 平方误差下的一次大偏差

prompt.en:
Emma compares two lines that predict bus travel time on the same four held-out trips. Their residuals (prediction minus measurement, in minutes) are:

Line A: 1, −1, 1, −1
Line B: 0, 0, 0, 3

Which statement is correct?
prompt.zh:
Emma 在同样四次留出的行程上比较两条预测公交行驶时间的直线。它们的残差（预测减实测，单位：分钟）是：

直线 A：1、−1、1、−1
直线 B：0、0、0、3

下列哪项说法正确？

text.en: Line A has the lower MSE: 1 against 2.25. Squaring makes B's single 3-minute miss cost 9.
text.zh: 直线 A 的 MSE 更低：1 对 2.25。平方使 B 那一次 3 分钟的偏差贡献了 9。

text.en: Line B has the lower MSE, because three of its four predictions are exact.
text.zh: 直线 B 的 MSE 更低，因为它四个预测中有三个完全准确。

why.en: Wrong. MSE does not count exact hits. It averages squared residuals, and one large residual dominates.
why.zh: 错误。MSE 不统计「完全命中」的次数，它平均的是残差的平方，一个大的残差会占主导。

text.en: Line A has MSE 0, because its residuals cancel out: 1 − 1 + 1 − 1 = 0.
text.zh: 直线 A 的 MSE 为 0，因为它的残差相互抵消：1 − 1 + 1 − 1 = 0。

why.en: Wrong. That is the mean signed residual. Squaring each residual first is exactly what stops positive and negative errors from cancelling.
why.zh: 错误。那是带符号残差的平均值。先把每个残差平方，恰恰就是为了不让正负误差相互抵消。

text.en: RMSE would rank the lines the other way, because the square root shrinks B's large error.
text.zh: 如果用 RMSE，排序会反过来，因为平方根会缩小 B 的大误差。

why.en: Wrong. The square root is applied to the whole MSE and keeps the order: RMSE is 1 for A and 1.5 for B.
why.zh: 错误。平方根作用在整个 MSE 上，不会改变顺序：A 的 RMSE 是 1，B 的是 1.5。

questions.verify_code:
import math
a = [1, -1, 1, -1]
b = [0, 0, 0, 3]
for name, r in [('A', a), ('B', b)]:
    mse = sum(x * x for x in r) / len(r)
    print(name, 'mean residual', sum(r) / len(r), 'MSE', mse, 'RMSE', math.sqrt(mse))
questions.verify_output:
A mean residual 0.0 MSE 1.0 RMSE 1.0
B mean residual 0.75 MSE 2.25 RMSE 1.5

title.en: RMSE of a print-time line
title.zh: 打印耗时直线的 RMSE

prompt.en:
Mia models print time in seconds from page count with the line ŷ = 5 + 2x. On four held-out jobs:

pages x: 2, 4, 6, 8
measured seconds y: 9, 13, 20, 22

What is the RMSE of the line on these jobs, in seconds? Give 3 decimal places.
prompt.zh:
Mia 用直线 ŷ = 5 + 2x 根据页数预测打印耗时（秒）。四个留出的打印任务如下：

页数 x：2、4、6、8
实测秒数 y：9、13、20、22

这条直线在这些任务上的 RMSE 是多少秒？保留 3 位小数。

solution.en:
Step 1: predictions. ŷ = 5 + 2 × 2 = 9, then 13, 17 and 21.

Step 2: residuals ŷ − y: 9 − 9 = 0, 13 − 13 = 0, 17 − 20 = −3, 21 − 22 = −1.

Step 3: squares are 0, 0, 9 and 1. Their sum is 10, so MSE = 10 / 4 = 2.5 squared seconds.

Step 4: RMSE = √2.5 = 1.581 seconds.

Meaning: a typical miss is about 1.6 seconds, and most of it comes from the 6-page job. For comparison, always predicting the mean of these targets (16 seconds) gives squared errors 49, 9, 16 and 36, MSE 27.5 and RMSE 5.244, so the line is far better here. Only the RMSE is in seconds; the MSE is in squared seconds.
solution.zh:
第 1 步：预测值。ŷ = 5 + 2 × 2 = 9，接着是 13、17、21。

第 2 步：残差 ŷ − y：9 − 9 = 0，13 − 13 = 0，17 − 20 = −3，21 − 22 = −1。

第 3 步：平方分别是 0、0、9、1，总和为 10，所以 MSE = 10 / 4 = 2.5（秒的平方）。

第 4 步：RMSE = √2.5 = 1.581 秒。

含义：典型偏差约为 1.6 秒，主要来自 6 页的那个任务。作为对比，始终预测这些目标的均值（16 秒）时，平方误差为 49、9、16、36，MSE 为 27.5，RMSE 为 5.244，所以这里直线要好得多。只有 RMSE 的单位是秒；MSE 的单位是秒的平方。

questions.verify_code:
import math
x = [2, 4, 6, 8]
y = [9, 13, 20, 22]
pred = [5 + 2 * v for v in x]
res = [p - t for p, t in zip(pred, y)]
mse = sum(r * r for r in res) / len(res)
print('pred', pred, 'res', res, 'mse', mse)
print(round(math.sqrt(mse), 4))

title.en: One gradient step on standardised inputs
title.zh: 在标准化输入上走一步梯度下降

prompt.en:
Jack fits ŷ = w·z + b with mean squared loss L = (1/n) Σ (w zᵢ + b − yᵢ)², where z is the standardised input.

Raw training inputs x: 1, 1, 5, 5
Targets y: 1, 3, 5, 7

Standardise x with the training mean and population standard deviation. Start at w = 0 and b = 0 with learning rate η = 0.1. Compute both gradients at the old values, update both parameters, and give the new training loss.
prompt.zh:
Jack 用均方损失 L = (1/n) Σ (w zᵢ + b − yᵢ)² 拟合 ŷ = w·z + b，其中 z 是标准化后的输入。

原始训练输入 x：1、1、5、5
目标 y：1、3、5、7

用训练均值和总体标准差把 x 标准化。从 w = 0、b = 0 出发，学习率 η = 0.1。先在旧参数处同时计算两个梯度，再更新两个参数，求更新后的训练损失。

solution.en:
Standardise. The mean of x is (1 + 1 + 5 + 5) / 4 = 3. Deviations are −2, −2, 2, 2, so the population standard deviation is √((4 + 4 + 4 + 4) / 4) = 2. z = −1, −1, 1, 1.

Start. All predictions are 0, so the errors ŷ − y are −1, −3, −5, −7 and L = (1 + 9 + 25 + 49) / 4 = 84 / 4 = 21.

Gradients (n = 4, so 2/n = 0.5):
g_w = 0.5 × [(−1)(−1) + (−3)(−1) + (−5)(1) + (−7)(1)] = 0.5 × (1 + 3 − 5 − 7) = 0.5 × (−8) = −4.
g_b = 0.5 × (−1 − 3 − 5 − 7) = 0.5 × (−16) = −8.

Update together: w = 0 − 0.1 × (−4) = 0.4 and b = 0 − 0.1 × (−8) = 0.8.

New loss. For z = −1 the prediction is −0.4 + 0.8 = 0.4; for z = 1 it is 0.4 + 0.8 = 1.2. Errors are 0.4 − 1 = −0.6, 0.4 − 3 = −2.6, 1.2 − 5 = −3.8 and 1.2 − 7 = −5.8. Squares: 0.36, 6.76, 14.44, 33.64. Sum 55.2, so L = 55.2 / 4 = 13.8.

One step cut the training loss from 21 to 13.8. That checks the update rule; it says nothing yet about new data.

questions.verify_code:
import numpy as np
x = np.array([1., 1., 5., 5.]); y = np.array([1., 3., 5., 7.])
z = (x - x.mean()) / x.std()
w, b, rate = 0., 0., 0.1
err = w * z + b - y
print('z', z.tolist(), 'start loss', np.mean(err ** 2))
gw = 2 * np.mean(err * z); gb = 2 * np.mean(err)
w, b = w - rate * gw, b - rate * gb
print('grads', gw, gb, 'params', round(w, 4), round(b, 4))
print(round(float(np.mean((w * z + b - y) ** 2)), 4))

title.en: Choose a threshold by validation cost
title.zh: 按验证集代价选择阈值

prompt.en:
Iris's fixed model gives the probability p that a clip contains a bird call, for 8 validation clips (table). A false alarm costs 1 (a person listens for nothing) and a missed bird call costs 3. She predicts "call" when p ≥ τ.

Candidate thresholds: τ = 0.25, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7. Which τ gives the lowest total cost on these clips? Enter the value of τ.
prompt.zh:
Iris 的模型（参数已固定）对 8 个验证片段给出了包含鸟叫的概率 p（见表）。一次误报的代价是 1（有人白听一次），一次漏报的代价是 3。当 p ≥ τ 时，她预测「有鸟叫」。

候选阈值：τ = 0.25、0.4、0.5、0.7。哪个 τ 在这些片段上的总代价最低？请填写 τ 的值。

solution.en:
Count false positives (FP) and false negatives (FN) at each threshold. Cost = 1 × FP + 3 × FN.

τ = 0.25: clips 2–8 are flagged. Calls found: 4, 6, 7, 8 (TP = 4). False alarms: 2, 3, 5 (FP = 3). Missed: none. Cost = 3 + 0 = 3.
τ = 0.4: clips 4–8 are flagged. TP = 4, FP = 1 (clip 5), FN = 0. Cost = 1.
τ = 0.5: clips 5–8 are flagged. TP = 3, FP = 1, FN = 1 (clip 4). Cost = 1 + 3 = 4.
τ = 0.7: clips 7 and 8 are flagged. TP = 2, FP = 0, FN = 2 (clips 4 and 6). Cost = 6.

The lowest cost is 1, at τ = 0.4.

The probabilities never changed; only the decision rule moved. Choose τ on validation clips like these, then report one result on a separate test set. Choosing τ on the test set would make that final score optimistic.
solution.zh:
在每个阈值下数出误报（FP）和漏报（FN）。代价 = 1 × FP + 3 × FN。

τ = 0.25：片段 2–8 被标记。找到的鸟叫：4、6、7、8（TP = 4）。误报：2、3、5（FP = 3）。漏报：无。代价 = 3 + 0 = 3。
τ = 0.4：片段 4–8 被标记。TP = 4，FP = 1（片段 5），FN = 0。代价 = 1。
τ = 0.5：片段 5–8 被标记。TP = 3，FP = 1，FN = 1（片段 4）。代价 = 1 + 3 = 4。
τ = 0.7：片段 7 和 8 被标记。TP = 2，FP = 0，FN = 2（片段 4 和 6）。代价 = 6。

最低代价是 1，对应 τ = 0.4。

概率从头到尾没有变，变的只是决策规则。应像这样在验证片段上选 τ，再在独立的测试集上报告一次结果。在测试集上选 τ 会让最终分数偏乐观。

title.en: What raising a threshold changes
title.zh: 提高阈值会改变什么

prompt.en: Leon's logistic-regression model is trained and fixed. He raises the decision threshold from 0.5 to 0.7 and scores the same validation set again. Which statement must be true?
prompt.zh: Leon 的逻辑回归模型已经训练好并固定下来。他把决策阈值从 0.5 提高到 0.7，并在同一个验证集上重新评分。下列哪项说法一定成立？

text.en: The predicted probabilities are unchanged, and the number of predicted positives cannot go up.
text.zh: 预测概率不变，并且被预测为正类的数量不会增加。

why.en: Right. The threshold is a separate decision rule. Any example with p ≥ 0.7 also had p ≥ 0.5, so the positive set can only shrink or stay the same.
why.zh: 正确。阈值是独立的决策规则。凡是 p ≥ 0.7 的样本也满足 p ≥ 0.5，所以正类集合只能缩小或保持不变。

text.en: Every predicted probability rises by 0.2.
text.zh: 每个预测概率都上升 0.2。

why.en: Wrong. Moving the threshold does not touch the weights or the probabilities, only the cut applied to them.
why.zh: 错误。移动阈值不会改变权重或概率，只改变作用在概率上的分界线。

text.en: Precision must go up.
text.zh: 精确率一定会上升。

why.en: Wrong. It often does, but not always: if the examples dropped (scores from 0.5 up to 0.7) contain a higher share of true positives than the ones that remain, precision falls. With no positives left it is undefined.
why.zh: 错误。它常常会上升，但并非总是如此：如果被去掉的那些 0.5 到 0.7 之间的样本中，真正例的比例高于留下的样本，精确率反而下降；如果一个正类预测都不剩，精确率就无法定义。

text.en: The model must be retrained, because its weights were fitted for a 0.5 threshold.
text.zh: 必须重新训练模型，因为它的权重是针对 0.5 的阈值拟合的。

why.en: Wrong. The weights are fitted to the training loss, not to a threshold. The same probabilities can be cut at any threshold.
why.zh: 错误。权重是根据训练损失拟合的，与阈值无关。同一组概率可以用任何阈值来切分。

title.en: F1 for a rare-defect detector
title.zh: 稀有缺陷检测器的 F1

prompt.en:
Emma tests a scratch detector on 200 parts: 16 are scratched and 184 are clean. The detector flags 20 parts, and 12 of the flagged parts really are scratched.

Treat "scratched" as the positive class. What is the detector's F1 score? Give 3 decimal places.
prompt.zh:
Emma 在 200 个零件上测试一个划痕检测器：16 个有划痕，184 个完好。检测器标记了 20 个零件，其中 12 个确实有划痕。

把「有划痕」当作正类。这个检测器的 F1 分数是多少？保留 3 位小数。

solution.en:
Build the counts first.
TP = 12 (flagged and scratched). FP = 20 − 12 = 8 (flagged but clean). FN = 16 − 12 = 4 (scratched but missed). TN = 184 − 8 = 176.

Precision = 12 / 20 = 0.60. Recall = 12 / 16 = 0.75.
F1 = 2 TP / (2 TP + FP + FN) = 24 / (24 + 8 + 4) = 24 / 36 = 0.667.

For comparison, accuracy is (12 + 176) / 200 = 0.94, while the "always clean" baseline already reaches 184 / 200 = 0.92 with recall 0. Accuracy hides most of the story here; the counts and F1 show how many scratches are found and how many clean parts are sent for review.
solution.zh:
先列出计数。
TP = 12（被标记且有划痕）。FP = 20 − 12 = 8（被标记但完好）。FN = 16 − 12 = 4（有划痕却漏掉）。TN = 184 − 8 = 176。

精确率 = 12 / 20 = 0.60。召回率 = 12 / 16 = 0.75。
F1 = 2 TP / (2 TP + FP + FN) = 24 / (24 + 8 + 4) = 24 / 36 = 0.667。

作为对比，准确率是 (12 + 176) / 200 = 0.94，而「全部判为完好」的基线已经达到 184 / 200 = 0.92，召回率却为 0。在这里准确率掩盖了大部分情况；计数和 F1 才能说明找到了多少划痕、又有多少完好零件被送去复查。

questions.verify_code:
tp, fp, fn = 12, 20 - 12, 16 - 12
tn = 184 - fp
print('counts', tp, fp, fn, tn)
print('precision', tp / (tp + fp), 'recall', tp / (tp + fn), 'accuracy', (tp + tn) / 200, 'baseline', 184 / 200)
print(round(2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn), 4))

title.en: Sweep a threshold: counts, precision, recall
title.zh: 扫描阈值：计数、精确率与召回率

prompt.en:
Noah's bird-call detector scored 10 validation clips, already sorted by score. 4 clips contain a call (label 1). The program predicts "call" when score ≥ t, for four thresholds.

Fill in TP, FP, FN, precision and recall for each threshold. Write precision and recall with 2 decimal places, exactly as the program prints them (for example 0.50 or 1.00). The first row is done for you.
prompt.zh:
Noah 的鸟叫检测器给 10 个验证片段打了分，片段已按分数排好序。其中 4 个片段含有鸟叫（标签为 1）。程序在 score ≥ t 时预测「有鸟叫」，共尝试四个阈值。

请为每个阈值填写 TP、FP、FN、精确率和召回率。精确率和召回率按程序的打印格式保留 2 位小数（例如 0.50 或 1.00）。第一行已经填好。

questions.code:
scores = [0.95, 0.85, 0.75, 0.65, 0.55, 0.45, 0.35, 0.25, 0.15, 0.05]
labels = [1,    0,    1,    1,    0,    0,    1,    0,    0,    0]
for t in [0.9, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3]:
    pred = [int(s >= t) for s in scores]
    tp = sum(p == 1 and y == 1 for p, y in zip(pred, labels))
    fp = sum(p == 1 and y == 0 for p, y in zip(pred, labels))
    fn = sum(p == 0 and y == 1 for p, y in zip(pred, labels))
    print(t, tp, fp, fn, f'{tp / (tp + fp):.2f}', f'{tp / (tp + fn):.2f}')

solution.en:
Read down the sorted list: lowering t only adds clips to the flagged set.

t = 0.7 flags the top three clips (labels 1, 0, 1): TP = 2, FP = 1, FN = 4 − 2 = 2. Precision = 2/3 = 0.67, recall = 2/4 = 0.50.
t = 0.5 adds 0.65 (call) and 0.55 (no call): TP = 3, FP = 2, FN = 1. Precision = 3/5 = 0.60, recall = 3/4 = 0.75.
t = 0.3 adds 0.45 (no call) and 0.35 (call): TP = 4, FP = 3, FN = 0. Precision = 4/7 = 0.571, printed 0.57; recall = 4/4 = 1.00.

What it shows: recall can only rise as t falls, while precision here falls from 1.00 to 0.57. F1 is 0.40, 0.57, 0.67 and 0.73, so it prefers t = 0.3, but that sends 7 clips to a listener to find 4 calls. Which threshold is right depends on the listening budget and on what a missed call costs, decided on validation data.
solution.zh:
沿着排好序的列表往下读：降低 t 只会往被标记集合里增加片段。

t = 0.7 标记前三个片段（标签为 1、0、1）：TP = 2，FP = 1，FN = 4 − 2 = 2。精确率 = 2/3 = 0.67，召回率 = 2/4 = 0.50。
t = 0.5 增加 0.65（有鸟叫）和 0.55（无鸟叫）：TP = 3，FP = 2，FN = 1。精确率 = 3/5 = 0.60，召回率 = 3/4 = 0.75。
t = 0.3 增加 0.45（无鸟叫）和 0.35（有鸟叫）：TP = 4，FP = 3，FN = 0。精确率 = 4/7 = 0.571，打印为 0.57；召回率 = 4/4 = 1.00。

这张表说明：t 降低时召回率只会上升，而这里的精确率从 1.00 降到 0.57。F1 依次为 0.40、0.57、0.67、0.73，所以 F1 偏向 t = 0.3，但那样要让人听 7 个片段才能找到 4 个鸟叫。哪个阈值合适，取决于收听的工作量和漏掉一次鸟叫的代价，并且要在验证数据上决定。

scores = [0.95, 0.85, 0.75, 0.65, 0.55, 0.45, 0.35, 0.25, 0.15, 0.05]
labels = [1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0]
for t in [0.9, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3]:
    pred = [int(s >= t) for s in scores]
    tp = sum(p == 1 and y == 1 for p, y in zip(pred, labels))
    fp = sum(p == 1 and y == 0 for p, y in zip(pred, labels))
    fn = sum(p == 0 and y == 1 for p, y in zip(pred, labels))
    print('\t'.join([str(t), str(tp), str(fp), str(fn), f'{tp / (tp + fp):.2f}', f'{tp / (tp + fn):.2f}']))

title.en: 3-NN before and after standardising
title.zh: 标准化前后的 3 近邻

prompt.en:
Jack predicts whether a delivery will be late (1) or on time (0) with 3-nearest neighbours and squared Euclidean distance. The table gives five training deliveries and one query.

First he uses the raw numbers. Then he standardises both features with the training means (600 m and 4 items) and population standard deviations (200 m and 2 items). What does 3-NN predict for the query each time?
prompt.zh:
Jack 用 3 近邻和平方欧氏距离预测一次送货会迟到（1）还是准时（0）。表格给出五次训练送货和一个查询。

他先直接使用原始数值。然后用训练均值（600 米、4 件）和总体标准差（200 米、2 件）把两个特征都标准化。两种情况下，3 近邻对查询分别预测什么？

questions.code:
Delivery  distance (m)  items  late?
D1            300          3      0
D2            500          5      1
D3            700          7      1
D4            900          1      0
D5            600          4      0
Query         620          1      ?

text.en: Raw: late (1). Standardised: on time (0).
text.zh: 原始数值：迟到（1）。标准化后：准时（0）。

why.en: Right. Raw distances are dominated by metres, so the neighbours are D5, D3 and D2 (labels 0, 1, 1). After standardising they are D4, D5 and D1 (labels 0, 0, 0).
why.zh: 正确。原始距离被「米」主导，邻居是 D5、D3、D2（标签 0、1、1）。标准化后邻居是 D4、D5、D1（标签 0、0、0）。

text.en: Raw: on time (0). Standardised: late (1).
text.zh: 原始数值：准时（0）。标准化后：迟到（1）。

why.en: Wrong. This reverses the two results. Work out the raw neighbours first: the items column adds at most 36 to a squared distance in the tens of thousands.
why.zh: 错误。这把两个结果弄反了。先算原始邻居：件数一列最多只给以万计的平方距离增加 36。

text.en: Late (1) both times. Standardising only changes the units, so the neighbours cannot change.
text.zh: 两次都是迟到（1）。标准化只是换了单位，邻居不会变。

why.en: Wrong. Each feature is divided by a different number (200 and 2), which changes how much each feature counts in the distance, and so changes the neighbours.
why.zh: 错误。每个特征除以的数不同（200 和 2），这改变了各特征在距离中的分量，因此邻居也会改变。

text.en: On time (0) both times, because the nearest delivery D5 is on time and the nearest one decides.
text.zh: 两次都是准时（0），因为最近的 D5 是准时的，由最近的那个决定。

why.en: Wrong. That is the 1-NN rule. With k = 3 the three nearest labels vote, and in the raw case two of them are late.
why.zh: 错误。那是 1 近邻的规则。k = 3 时由最近三个标签投票，原始数值下其中两个是迟到。

solution.en:
Raw squared distances to the query (620 m, 1 item):
D1: 320² + 2² = 102404. D2: 120² + 4² = 14416. D3: 80² + 6² = 6436. D4: 280² + 0² = 78400. D5: 20² + 3² = 409.
Nearest three: D5, D3, D2 with labels 0, 1, 1. Mean 2/3 > 1/2, so the prediction is late.

Standardised. Subtracting a mean cancels inside a difference, so divide the raw differences by 200 and by 2:
D1: (320/200)² + (2/2)² = 2.56 + 1 = 3.56. D2: 0.6² + 2² = 4.36. D3: 0.4² + 3² = 9.16. D4: 1.4² + 0² = 1.96. D5: 0.1² + 1.5² = 2.26.
Nearest three: D4, D5, D1 with labels 0, 0, 0, so the prediction is on time.

Which map is "right" is a modelling choice, but the raw one silently ignores the number of items. Fit the scaling on training data and choose k on validation data.
solution.zh:
查询（620 米，1 件）的原始平方距离：
D1：320² + 2² = 102404。D2：120² + 4² = 14416。D3：80² + 6² = 6436。D4：280² + 0² = 78400。D5：20² + 3² = 409。
最近的三个是 D5、D3、D2，标签为 0、1、1。平均值 2/3 > 1/2，所以预测为迟到。

标准化后。减去均值在差值中会相互抵消，所以只需把原始差值分别除以 200 和 2：
D1：(320/200)² + (2/2)² = 2.56 + 1 = 3.56。D2：0.6² + 2² = 4.36。D3：0.4² + 3² = 9.16。D4：1.4² + 0² = 1.96。D5：0.1² + 1.5² = 2.26。
最近的三个是 D4、D5、D1，标签为 0、0、0，所以预测为准时。

哪种「地图」更合理是建模选择，但原始数值实际上悄悄忽略了件数。缩放要用训练数据拟合，k 要用验证数据选择。

questions.verify_code:
import numpy as np
x = np.array([[300, 3], [500, 5], [700, 7], [900, 1], [600, 4]], float)
y = np.array([0, 1, 1, 0, 0])
q = np.array([620, 1.])
mean, sd = x.mean(axis=0), x.std(axis=0)
print('mean', mean.tolist(), 'sd', sd.tolist())
for name, a, b in [('raw', x, q), ('scaled', (x - mean) / sd, (q - mean) / sd)]:
    d = ((a - b) ** 2).sum(axis=1)
    near = np.argsort(d, kind='stable')[:3]
    print(name, np.round(d, 4).tolist(), (near + 1).tolist(), int(y[near].mean() > 0.5))

title.en: Naive Bayes with smoothing and unequal priors
title.zh: 带平滑与不等先验的朴素贝叶斯

prompt.en:
Emma's spam filter uses multinomial naive Bayes over the vocabulary [win, prize, meeting], so V = 3. Training word counts:

spam: win 4, prize 3, meeting 0 (7 words in total)
ordinary: win 1, prize 0, meeting 5 (6 words in total)

Class priors: P(spam) = 0.3, P(ordinary) = 0.7. A new message is "win prize". Using add-one smoothing, what is the model's P(spam | message)? Give 3 decimal places.
prompt.zh:
Emma 的垃圾消息过滤器在词表 [win, prize, meeting] 上使用多项式朴素贝叶斯，所以 V = 3。训练中的词计数为：

spam：win 4，prize 3，meeting 0（共 7 个词）
ordinary：win 1，prize 0，meeting 5（共 6 个词）

类别先验：P(spam) = 0.3，P(ordinary) = 0.7。一条新消息是「win prize」。使用加一平滑，模型给出的 P(spam | 消息) 是多少？保留 3 位小数。

solution.en:
Smoothed word probabilities θ = (count + 1) / (class total + V).
spam: win (4 + 1) / (7 + 3) = 0.5; prize (3 + 1) / 10 = 0.4; meeting 1 / 10 = 0.1.
ordinary: win (1 + 1) / (6 + 3) = 2/9 ≈ 0.2222; prize (0 + 1) / 9 = 1/9 ≈ 0.1111; meeting 6/9.

Unnormalised scores for "win prize" (each word once):
spam: 0.3 × 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.06.
ordinary: 0.7 × 2/9 × 1/9 = 0.7 × 2/81 ≈ 0.01728.

Normalise: P(spam | message) = 0.06 / (0.06 + 0.01728) = 0.06 / 0.07728 ≈ 0.776.

The same in logs: spam ln 0.3 + ln 0.5 + ln 0.4 = −1.204 − 0.693 − 0.916 = −2.813; ordinary ln 0.7 + ln(2/9) + ln(1/9) = −0.357 − 1.504 − 2.197 = −4.058. exp(−2.813) / (exp(−2.813) + exp(−4.058)) gives the same 0.776.

Without smoothing, prize has probability 0 in ordinary messages, so P(spam) would be exactly 1: one unseen word would wipe out the other class. The prior of 0.7 for ordinary pulls the answer down from what equal priors would give (0.890).
solution.zh:
平滑后的词概率 θ = (计数 + 1) / (类别词总数 + V)。
spam：win (4 + 1) / (7 + 3) = 0.5；prize (3 + 1) / 10 = 0.4；meeting 1 / 10 = 0.1。
ordinary：win (1 + 1) / (6 + 3) = 2/9 ≈ 0.2222；prize (0 + 1) / 9 = 1/9 ≈ 0.1111；meeting 6/9。

「win prize」的未归一化得分（每个词出现一次）：
spam：0.3 × 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.06。
ordinary：0.7 × 2/9 × 1/9 = 0.7 × 2/81 ≈ 0.01728。

归一化：P(spam | 消息) = 0.06 / (0.06 + 0.01728) = 0.06 / 0.07728 ≈ 0.776。

用对数计算结果相同：spam 为 ln 0.3 + ln 0.5 + ln 0.4 = −1.204 − 0.693 − 0.916 = −2.813；ordinary 为 ln 0.7 + ln(2/9) + ln(1/9) = −0.357 − 1.504 − 2.197 = −4.058。exp(−2.813) / (exp(−2.813) + exp(−4.058)) 同样得到 0.776。

如果不做平滑，prize 在 ordinary 中的概率是 0，P(spam) 就会恰好等于 1：一个没见过的词就能抹掉另一个类别。ordinary 的先验 0.7 把答案往下拉了；如果两个先验相等，结果会是 0.890。

title.en: Gini reduction of one split
title.zh: 一次划分的基尼不纯度下降量

prompt.en:
Noah's decision-tree node holds 12 kite flights: 6 stayed up (positive) and 6 fell. The split "wind below 4 m/s?" sends 5 flights left (4 positive, 1 not) and 7 flights right (2 positive, 5 not).

Use binary Gini impurity G(p) = 2p(1 − p). What is the impurity reduction ΔG of this split? Give 3 decimal places.
prompt.zh:
Noah 的决策树节点里有 12 次风筝放飞记录：6 次保持在空中（正类），6 次掉落。划分「风速低于 4 m/s？」把 5 次放飞分到左边（4 次正类，1 次不是），7 次分到右边（2 次正类，5 次不是）。

使用二分类基尼不纯度 G(p) = 2p(1 − p)。这次划分的不纯度下降量 ΔG 是多少？保留 3 位小数。

solution.en:
Parent: p = 6/12 = 0.5, so G = 2 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.5.

Left child: p = 4/5 = 0.8, so G = 2 × 0.8 × 0.2 = 0.32.
Right child: p = 2/7 ≈ 0.2857, so G = 2 × (2/7) × (5/7) = 20/49 ≈ 0.4082.

Weighted child impurity = (5/12) × 0.32 + (7/12) × 0.4082 = 0.1333 + 0.2381 = 0.3714.

ΔG = 0.5 − 0.3714 = 0.1286, which rounds to 0.129.

Meaning: on average the children are purer than the parent by 0.129. The weights matter: the larger right child counts for 7/12 of the result. A positive ΔG is a local improvement on training data, not proof that the tree will do better on new flights.

questions.verify_code:
def gini(pos, n):
    p = pos / n
    return 2 * p * (1 - p)
parent = gini(6, 12)
left, right = gini(4, 5), gini(2, 7)
child = 5 / 12 * left + 7 / 12 * right
print(parent, left, round(right, 4), round(child, 4))
print(round(parent - child, 4))

title.en: Average probabilities or count votes?
title.zh: 平均概率还是统计投票？

prompt.en:
Five trees in Jack's forest give these positive-class probabilities for one new flight:

0.45, 0.45, 0.45, 0.90, 0.95

The decision threshold is 0.5. Which statement is correct?
prompt.zh:
Jack 的随机森林中有五棵树，它们对一次新的放飞给出的正类概率是：

0.45、0.45、0.45、0.90、0.95

决策阈值是 0.5。下列哪项说法正确？

text.en: Averaging gives 0.64, so the forest says positive; a majority vote of the five thresholded labels says negative (2 of 5). The combination rule must be stated.
text.zh: 取平均得 0.64，所以森林判为正类；而对五棵树先按阈值判定再多数投票，结果是负类（5 票中 2 票）。必须说明采用哪种组合规则。

why.en: Right. (0.45 × 3 + 0.90 + 0.95) / 5 = 3.2 / 5 = 0.64 ≥ 0.5. Only two trees are above 0.5 on their own, so a vote gives 2 against 3.

text.en: Both rules always agree, because they use the same five trees.
text.zh: 两种规则总是一致的，因为它们用的是同样五棵树。

why.en: Wrong. Here they disagree: averaging keeps how confident each tree is, while a vote throws that away.
why.zh: 错误。这里两者就不一致：取平均保留了每棵树的把握程度，而投票把它丢掉了。

text.en: Averaging gives 0.45, the middle value, so the forest says negative.
text.zh: 取平均得 0.45，也就是中间的那个值，所以森林判为负类。

why.en: Wrong. 0.45 is the median. The forest rule in the chapter is the mean of the probabilities, 0.64.
why.zh: 错误。0.45 是中位数。本章的森林规则是概率的平均值，即 0.64。

text.en: Both rules say positive, because the two very confident trees outweigh the other three in a vote too.
text.zh: 两种规则都判为正类，因为在投票中，两棵把握很大的树同样能压过另外三棵。

why.en: Wrong. In a vote each tree has one equal vote, whatever its confidence, so the result is 2 positive against 3 negative.
why.zh: 错误。投票时每棵树不论把握多大都只有一票，所以结果是 2 票正类对 3 票负类。

questions.verify_code:
p = [0.45, 0.45, 0.45, 0.90, 0.95]
mean = sum(p) / len(p)
votes = sum(x >= 0.5 for x in p)
print(round(mean, 4), int(mean >= 0.5), votes, int(votes > len(p) / 2))

title.en: Two rounds of residual boosting
title.zh: 两轮残差提升

prompt.en:
Mia predicts robot task durations (minutes). Four training tasks have x = 1, 2, 3, 4 and targets y = 2, 4, 6, 12.

Start with F₀ = the training mean. Each round fits a stump to the residuals r = y − F (each leaf predicts the mean residual of its rows) and adds η = 0.5 times the stump's output.
Round 1 splits x ≤ 2 from x ≥ 3. Round 2 splits x ≤ 3 from x = 4.

What is the training MSE after round 2? Give 4 decimal places.
prompt.zh:
Mia 要预测机器人任务的耗时（分钟）。四个训练任务的 x = 1、2、3、4，目标 y = 2、4、6、12。

从 F₀ = 训练均值开始。每一轮用一个树桩拟合残差 r = y − F（每片叶子预测该叶子中各行残差的平均值），再把树桩输出的 η = 0.5 倍加到预测上。
第 1 轮把 x ≤ 2 与 x ≥ 3 分开。第 2 轮把 x ≤ 3 与 x = 4 分开。

第 2 轮之后的训练 MSE 是多少？保留 4 位小数。

solution.en:
Start. F₀ = (2 + 4 + 6 + 12) / 4 = 6. Residuals r = −4, −2, 0, 6. MSE = (16 + 4 + 0 + 36) / 4 = 14.

Round 1. Left leaf (x ≤ 2): (−4 − 2) / 2 = −3. Right leaf: (0 + 6) / 2 = 3.
F₁ = 6 + 0.5 × (−3, −3, 3, 3) = 4.5, 4.5, 7.5, 7.5.
New residuals y − F₁ = −2.5, −0.5, −1.5, 4.5. MSE = (6.25 + 0.25 + 2.25 + 20.25) / 4 = 29 / 4 = 7.25.

Round 2. Left leaf (x ≤ 3): (−2.5 − 0.5 − 1.5) / 3 = −1.5. Right leaf (x = 4): 4.5.
F₂ = F₁ + 0.5 × (−1.5, −1.5, −1.5, 4.5) = 3.75, 3.75, 6.75, 9.75.

Errors F₂ − y: 1.75, −0.25, 0.75, −2.25. Squares: 3.0625, 0.0625, 0.5625, 5.0625. Sum 8.75, so MSE = 8.75 / 4 = 2.1875.

Training MSE fell 14 → 7.25 → 2.1875. Each round repaired part of what was left. The 12-minute task pulls hard on every round because squared error weights it heavily. A falling training loss does not choose the number of rounds; watch validation error for that.

questions.verify_code:
import numpy as np
y = np.array([2., 4., 6., 12.])
F = np.full(4, y.mean())
print('MSE0', np.mean((F - y) ** 2))
for left in ([True, True, False, False], [True, True, True, False]):
    left = np.array(left)
    r = y - F
    stump = np.where(left, r[left].mean(), r[~left].mean())
    F = F + 0.5 * stump
    print('residual', r.tolist(), 'F', F.tolist(), 'MSE', np.mean((F - y) ** 2))
print(np.mean((F - y) ** 2))

title.en: One k-means round and its objective
title.zh: 一轮 k 均值及其目标函数

prompt.en:
Iris clusters six stone lengths (cm): 1, 2, 4, 9, 10, 12. She runs k-means with k = 2, starting centres 2 and 10.

Do one assignment step and one update step. Then compute J, the sum of squared distances from each point to its assigned, updated centre. Give 3 decimal places.
prompt.zh:
Iris 对六块石头的长度（厘米）做聚类：1、2、4、9、10、12。她用 k = 2 运行 k 均值，初始中心为 2 和 10。

先做一次分配步骤和一次更新步骤，然后计算 J：每个点到其所属（更新后的）中心的平方距离之和。保留 3 位小数。

solution.en:
Assignment. Each point goes to the nearer centre. 1 and 2 are nearer 2. For 4: |4 − 2| = 2 and |4 − 10| = 6, so it joins centre 2. 9, 10 and 12 join centre 10.

Update. c₁ = (1 + 2 + 4) / 3 = 7/3 ≈ 2.333. c₂ = (9 + 10 + 12) / 3 = 31/3 ≈ 10.333.

Objective.
Group 1: (1 − 2.333)² + (2 − 2.333)² + (4 − 2.333)² = 1.778 + 0.111 + 2.778 = 4.667.
Group 2: (9 − 10.333)² + (10 − 10.333)² + (12 − 10.333)² = 1.778 + 0.111 + 2.778 = 4.667.
J = 4.667 + 4.667 = 9.333 (exactly 28/3).

For scale: one centre at the overall mean 38/6 ≈ 6.333 gives J ≈ 105.333. Two groups reduce J a lot, but J always falls when k grows, so a small J alone does not prove there are two kinds of stone.

questions.verify_code:
pts = [1, 2, 4, 9, 10, 12]
centres = [2, 10]
groups = [[p for p in pts if abs(p - centres[0]) <= abs(p - centres[1])],
          [p for p in pts if abs(p - centres[0]) > abs(p - centres[1])]]
new = [sum(g) / len(g) for g in groups]
J = sum((p - c) ** 2 for g, c in zip(groups, new) for p in g)
one = sum((p - sum(pts) / 6) ** 2 for p in pts)
print(groups, [round(c, 4) for c in new], round(one, 4))
print(round(J, 4))

title.en: PCA after a change of units
title.zh: 换单位之后的 PCA

prompt.en: Leon runs PCA on stones described by length and mass. On the training stones, the variance of length is 4 cm² and the variance of mass is 0.09 kg², with almost no covariance between them. He then records mass in grams instead of kilograms. Which statement is correct?
prompt.zh: Leon 对用长度和质量描述的石头做 PCA。在训练石头上，长度的方差是 4 cm²，质量的方差是 0.09 kg²，两者之间几乎没有协方差。随后他改用克而不是千克记录质量。下列哪项说法正确？

text.en: In kilograms the first component points along length (about 98% of the variance). In grams the mass variance becomes 90,000 g², so the first component switches to mass. Choose and state a scaling rule before PCA.
text.zh: 以千克为单位时，第一主成分沿长度方向（约占方差的 98%）。改用克之后，质量的方差变成 90,000 g²，第一主成分就转到质量方向。做 PCA 之前要选定并写明缩放规则。

why.en: Right. Variance scales with the square of the unit: 0.09 × 1000² = 90,000. Shares: 4 / 4.09 ≈ 0.978 in kilograms, and 90,000 / 90,004 ≈ 1.000 for mass in grams.

text.en: PCA does not depend on units, because it subtracts the mean before anything else.
text.zh: PCA 与单位无关，因为它先减去均值。

why.en: Wrong. Centring removes the offset, not the scale. The spread of each coordinate still depends on its unit.
why.zh: 错误。中心化去掉的是偏移，而不是尺度。每个坐标的离散程度仍然取决于它的单位。

text.en: The first component always points along the feature that best separates the rock types.
text.zh: 第一主成分总是指向最能区分岩石类型的那个特征。

why.en: Wrong. PCA never sees rock-type labels. It finds the direction of largest spread, which may be nuisance variation.
why.zh: 错误。PCA 根本看不到岩石类型的标签。它找的是离散程度最大的方向，而那可能只是无关的变化。

text.en: Changing units changes the covariance between the features but leaves each variance the same.
text.zh: 换单位会改变特征之间的协方差，但每个特征的方差保持不变。

why.en: Wrong. Multiplying mass by 1000 multiplies its variance by 1000² and the covariance by 1000.
why.zh: 错误。质量乘以 1000，其方差乘以 1000²，协方差乘以 1000。

questions.verify_code:
for name, mass_var in [('kg', 0.09), ('g', 0.09 * 1000 ** 2)]:
    total = 4 + mass_var
    first = 'length' if 4 > mass_var else 'mass'
    print(name, round(mass_var, 2), first, round(max(4, mass_var) / total, 4))

title.en: Cosine similarity changes the ranking
title.zh: 余弦相似度改变了排序

prompt.en:
Emma's viewer profile is u = [2, 1, 0] over the features (astronomy, robotics, chemistry). Three videos have feature vectors:

A = [1, 0, 0]
B = [2, 1, 2]
C = [0, 1, 0]

What is the cosine similarity between B and the profile? Give 3 decimal places. (Then compare the ranking by dot product with the ranking by cosine.)
prompt.zh:
Emma 的观众画像是 u = [2, 1, 0]，三个特征依次为（天文、机器人、化学）。三个视频的特征向量是：

A = [1, 0, 0]
B = [2, 1, 2]
C = [0, 1, 0]

B 与画像之间的余弦相似度是多少？保留 3 位小数。（然后比较按点积排序与按余弦排序的结果。）

solution.en:
Length of the profile: ‖u‖ = √(4 + 1 + 0) = √5 ≈ 2.236.

B: u·B = 2×2 + 1×1 + 0×2 = 5. ‖B‖ = √(4 + 1 + 4) = 3. cos = 5 / (2.236 × 3) = 5 / 6.708 ≈ 0.745.

The other two, for the ranking:
A: u·A = 2, ‖A‖ = 1, cos = 2 / 2.236 ≈ 0.894.
C: u·C = 1, ‖C‖ = 1, cos = 1 / 2.236 ≈ 0.447.

By dot product the order is B (5), A (2), C (1). By cosine it is A (0.894), B (0.745), C (0.447). B's large chemistry tag makes it long, which helps its dot product, but it also points away from the profile, which cosine penalises. Neither score is a probability that the viewer will enjoy the video.

title.en: Repair a validation plan for café sales
title.zh: 修正一份咖啡店销量的验证方案

prompt.en:
Jack predicts a café's daily sales from weather, weekday and holiday flags, using linear regression with an L2 penalty. He has two years of daily rows (730 days). His plan:

1. Standardise every feature with the mean and standard deviation of all 730 days.
2. Run 5-fold cross-validation with folds drawn at random from all days, trying 20 values of the penalty strength λ.
3. Report the best mean cross-validation error as the final result.

Next month the café starts a new menu and longer opening hours.

(a) Name three problems with this plan.
(b) Describe a corrected protocol.
(c) What should Jack do after the menu change?
prompt.zh:
Jack 用带 L2 惩罚的线性回归，根据天气、星期几和节假日标记预测一家咖啡店的每日销量。他有两年的逐日数据（730 天）。他的方案是：

1. 用全部 730 天的均值和标准差把每个特征标准化。
2. 从全部日期中随机抽取，做 5 折交叉验证，尝试 20 个惩罚强度 λ。
3. 把最好的交叉验证平均误差作为最终结果报告。

下个月，咖啡店将推出新菜单并延长营业时间。

(a) 指出这个方案的三个问题。
(b) 描述一个修正后的方案。
(c) 菜单改变之后，Jack 应该做什么？

solution.en:
(a) Problems.
- Scaling leak: the means and standard deviations come from all 730 days, including the days used for validation. They must be fitted inside each training portion only.
- Random folds ignore time: daily sales have seasons and trends. Training on later days to predict earlier ones answers an easier question than "tomorrow", so the error is optimistic.
- No untouched final test: the same folds chose λ out of 20 candidates, so the best cross-validation error is a selection score, not an honest final estimate.

(b) Corrected protocol.
- Reserve the most recent period (for example the last two months) as the final test and do not look at it.
- On the earlier data, use time-ordered validation: train on months 1 to k, validate on month k + 1, and repeat for several k. Fit the scaler inside each training portion.
- Choose λ by the mean validation error. Refit the chosen setting on all development data, then evaluate once on the final period. Compare with a simple baseline, such as "same weekday last week".

(c) After the change.
- Treat the new menu and opening hours as a distribution shift: the old test score is no longer a promise.
- Watch the inputs (for example new opening hours or fields that start going missing) and, above all, collect fresh labelled days and compare the error on them with the old error, broken down by weekday.
- Retrain or adapt when there is enough new data, and validate the update on later days before trusting it. Regularisation alone does not protect against this change.
solution.zh:
(a) 问题。
- 缩放泄漏：均值和标准差来自全部 730 天，其中包括用于验证的日期。它们只能在每个训练部分内部拟合。
- 随机折忽略了时间：每日销量有季节和趋势。用较晚的日期训练、预测较早的日期，回答的问题比「预测明天」容易，所以误差偏乐观。
- 没有未动过的最终测试：同样的折从 20 个候选值中选出了 λ，所以最好的交叉验证误差只是选择用的分数，而不是诚实的最终估计。

(b) 修正后的方案。
- 把最近的一段时间（例如最后两个月）留作最终测试，并且不去看它。
- 在较早的数据上做按时间顺序的验证：用第 1 到第 k 个月训练，用第 k + 1 个月验证，对几个不同的 k 重复。缩放器在每个训练部分内部拟合。
- 按平均验证误差选择 λ。用全部开发数据重新拟合选定的设置，然后在最终时间段上只评估一次。并与简单基线比较，例如「上周同一天的销量」。

(c) 菜单改变之后。
- 把新菜单和营业时间看作分布偏移：旧的测试分数不再是保证。
- 监控输入（例如新的营业时间，或开始出现缺失的字段），更重要的是收集新的有标签日期，把它们上的误差与旧误差比较，并按星期几分开看。
- 有了足够的新数据后再重新训练或调整，并且先在更晚的日期上验证这次更新，然后才信任它。仅靠正则化并不能抵御这种变化。

text.en: Identifies the scaling leak: statistics from all days, including validation days; fit inside each training portion.
text.zh: 指出缩放泄漏：统计量来自全部日期（包括验证日期）；应在每个训练部分内部拟合。

text.en: Identifies that random folds ignore time order, making the estimate optimistic for forecasting.
text.zh: 指出随机折忽略了时间顺序，使预测未来的误差估计偏乐观。

text.en: Identifies that the best of 20 cross-validation scores is a selection score, not a final test result.
text.zh: 指出 20 个交叉验证分数中的最好值只是选择用的分数，而不是最终测试结果。

text.en: Proposes time-ordered validation (training before validation period) with preprocessing fitted inside each training portion.
text.zh: 提出按时间顺序的验证（训练期在验证期之前），预处理在每个训练部分内部拟合。

text.en: Reserves an untouched final period, refits the chosen λ on development data and evaluates once.
text.zh: 保留一段未动过的最终时间段，用开发数据重新拟合选定的 λ，并只评估一次。

text.en: After the menu change: treats it as a shift, collects fresh labelled days and re-evaluates before trusting the old score.
text.zh: 菜单改变后：把它当作分布偏移，收集新的有标签日期，在信任旧分数之前重新评估。

mistakes.en: Claiming that a stronger L2 penalty will protect the model against the menu change.
mistakes.zh: 声称更强的 L2 惩罚能让模型抵御菜单变化。

mistakes.en: Using the final test period to choose λ.
mistakes.zh: 用最终测试时间段来选择 λ。

mistakes.en: Shuffling the days "so that every fold sees every season", which is exactly the leak to avoid.
mistakes.zh: 为了「让每一折都覆盖每个季节」而打乱日期，而这恰恰是要避免的泄漏。

title.en: An input change is not an accuracy measurement
title.zh: 输入变化不等于准确率测量

prompt.en: Noah monitors a message classifier. After an update to the email importer, the share of messages with a missing "sender domain" field rose from 2% to 30% within a week. No new labels have been collected yet. Which conclusion is best supported?
prompt.zh: Noah 在监控一个消息分类器。邮件导入程序更新后的一周内，缺少「发件人域名」字段的消息比例从 2% 上升到 30%。目前还没有收集任何新的标签。下列哪个结论最有依据？

text.en: The inputs have changed. Inspect the importer first, and collect fresh labels before claiming that accuracy has fallen.
text.zh: 输入发生了变化。应先检查导入程序，并在断言准确率下降之前先收集新的标签。

why.en: Right. A rise in missing values is a warning about the inputs, and a parsing fault is the first suspect. Only fresh labels can show whether the predictions got worse.
why.zh: 正确。缺失值上升是关于输入的警告，解析故障是首要嫌疑。只有新的标签才能说明预测是否变差。

text.en: Accuracy has fallen by 28 percentage points.
text.zh: 准确率下降了 28 个百分点。

why.en: Wrong. 28 points is the change in the missing-field rate, not in accuracy. Without labels the accuracy change is unknown.
why.zh: 错误。28 个百分点是字段缺失率的变化，而不是准确率的变化。没有标签就不知道准确率变了多少。

text.en: Nothing important changed, because the average predicted probability is still 0.4.
text.zh: 没有发生重要变化，因为平均预测概率仍然是 0.4。

why.en: Wrong. A stable summary of the outputs does not guarantee that individual predictions, or the input–label relationship, are unchanged.
why.zh: 错误。输出的汇总值稳定，并不能保证单个预测或输入与标签之间的关系没有变化。

text.en: Recalibrate the probabilities on the final test set straight away.
text.zh: 立即在最终测试集上重新校准概率。

why.en: Wrong. Recalibration needs separate data, and fitting it on the final test set contaminates the evaluation. The importer fault may also be the real problem.
why.zh: 错误。重新校准需要单独的数据，在最终测试集上拟合会污染评估。而且真正的问题可能是导入程序的故障。

title.en: Brier score of an over-confident bin
title.zh: 一个过度自信分箱的布里尔分数

prompt.en: Iris's filter gave five recently labelled messages the same spam probability, 0.9. Their true labels are 1, 1, 1, 0, 0 (1 = spam). What is the Brier score on these five messages?
prompt.zh: Iris 的过滤器给最近五条已标注的消息都打出了相同的垃圾消息概率 0.9。它们的真实标签是 1、1、1、0、0（1 表示垃圾消息）。这五条消息上的布里尔分数是多少？

solution.en:
The bin's mean prediction is 0.9, but the observed spam fraction is 3/5 = 0.6, so the filter is over-confident here by 0.3.

Squared errors (p − y)²: for the three spam messages (0.9 − 1)² = 0.01 each, total 0.03; for the two ordinary ones (0.9 − 0)² = 0.81 each, total 1.62.

Brier = (0.03 + 1.62) / 5 = 1.65 / 5 = 0.33. Lower is better.

For comparison, predicting 0.6 for all five would give (3 × 0.16 + 2 × 0.36) / 5 = 0.24 on these labels. But five messages are far too few for a precise calibration claim, and any recalibration must be fitted on data separate from the final test.
solution.zh:
这个分箱的平均预测是 0.9，而观测到的垃圾消息比例是 3/5 = 0.6，所以过滤器在这里过度自信了 0.3。

平方误差 (p − y)²：三条垃圾消息每条为 (0.9 − 1)² = 0.01，合计 0.03；两条普通消息每条为 (0.9 − 0)² = 0.81，合计 1.62。

布里尔分数 = (0.03 + 1.62) / 5 = 1.65 / 5 = 0.33。越低越好。

作为对比，如果对五条消息都预测 0.6，在这些标签上会得到 (3 × 0.16 + 2 × 0.36) / 5 = 0.24。不过五条消息远远不足以得出精确的校准结论，而且任何重新校准都必须在独立于最终测试的数据上拟合。

questions.verify_code:
p = [0.9] * 5
y = [1, 1, 1, 0, 0]
print('mean p', sum(p) / 5, 'observed', sum(y) / 5)
print('constant 0.6', round(sum((0.6 - t) ** 2 for t in y) / 5, 4))
print(round(sum((a - b) ** 2 for a, b in zip(p, y)) / 5, 4))

title.en: Leakage in cross-validation: fit inside the folds
title.zh: 交叉验证中的数据泄漏：把拟合放进折内

summary.en: A scaler and a feature selector are fitted on all rows before cross-validation. The score looks excellent, survives shuffled labels, and does not survive a new batch. A Pipeline fixes it.
summary.zh: 在交叉验证之前，用全部数据拟合了缩放器和特征选择器。分数看起来极好，标签打乱后依然很高，换一批新数据就不成立。用 Pipeline 修复。

scenario.en:
Mia's team is building a go/no-go model for a burn-in test: each unit gets 500 sensor summaries (temperatures, ripple, drift, all in different units), and the label says whether it later failed. They have 150 labelled units. Jack must decide whether to commit the test rig to the model, so the question is simple: how well will it do on the next batch?

The team's script reports a cross-validated ROC AUC, and the number is very good. Iris, the reviewer, asks one question: what does the script report if the labels are shuffled? The lab follows that question. You will see that the good number is produced by the order of two lines of preprocessing, not by the sensors, and what that would have cost after deployment. All data is fabricated by a seeded generator, and nothing heavy is trained: every run takes a second or two.
scenario.zh:
Mia 的团队在为老化测试做一个“放行/拦截”模型：每个单元有 500 个传感器汇总值（温度、纹波、漂移，单位各不相同），标签表示它之后是否失效。他们手上有 150 个带标签的单元。Jack 要决定是否让测试台依赖这个模型，所以问题很简单：它在下一批上会表现如何？

团队的脚本报告了交叉验证的 ROC AUC，数字很好。评审人 Iris 只问了一个问题：如果把标签打乱，脚本会报告什么？这个实验就沿着这个问题走。你会看到，这个好数字来自两行预处理代码的先后顺序，而不是传感器本身；你还会看到，如果带着它上线，会付出什么代价。所有数据都由带种子的生成器编造，不训练任何大模型：每次运行只要一两秒。

title.en: Run the team's script
title.zh: 运行团队的脚本

body.en:
ROC AUC is the probability that the model ranks a randomly chosen failing unit above a randomly chosen passing one: 0.5 is a coin flip and 1.0 is perfect. `cross_val_score` splits the rows into folds, trains on all but one, scores the held-out fold, and repeats. `RepeatedStratifiedKFold` keeps the failing share the same in every fold and repeats the whole 5-fold split three times with different shuffles, so one lucky split cannot decide the result; `random_state=0` fixes the shuffles. The script prints the mean and the spread over the 15 folds.

Before you look at the number, read `prepare` and `cv_estimate` in `train.py` and write down the order of operations. Scaling sees every row. Selection sees every row and every label. Only then does cross-validation start.
body.zh:
ROC AUC 是模型把随机挑出的一个失效单元排在随机挑出的一个正常单元之前的概率：0.5 相当于抛硬币，1.0 是完美。`cross_val_score` 把行分成若干折，用其余折训练、在留出的那一折上打分，然后轮流重复。`RepeatedStratifiedKFold` 让每一折里失效单元的比例保持一致，并用不同的洗牌把整个 5 折划分重复三次，这样一次运气好的划分不能决定结果；`random_state=0` 固定了洗牌。脚本打印 15 折的均值和离散程度。

看数字之前，先读 `train.py` 里的 `prepare` 和 `cv_estimate`，写下操作的顺序：缩放看到了每一行；特征选择看到了每一行以及每一个标签；这之后交叉验证才开始。

steps.output:
150 units, 500 sensors, 75 failures
cross-validated ROC AUC: 0.825 (std 0.042 over 15 folds)

title.en: Run the control that should be boring
title.zh: 运行本该毫无亮点的对照实验

body.en:
`--shuffle-labels` randomly reassigns the labels, so no relation between sensors and failures remains. A sound procedure must then report about 0.5. The control averages five different shuffles so one unlucky shuffle cannot mislead.

If the score stays far above 0.5 here, the evaluation is leaking information from the labels into the part of the pipeline that should not see them. There is nothing to be learned, yet the procedure reports learning. That is not a good model. It is a defect in the measurement.
body.zh:
`--shuffle-labels` 随机重新分配标签，传感器与失效之间不再有任何关系。此时正确的流程必须报告约 0.5。对照实验取五次不同打乱的平均，避免一次倒霉的打乱造成误导。

如果这里的分数仍远高于 0.5，说明评估把标签信息泄漏给了本不该看到它们的那部分流程。明明没有可学的东西，流程却报告学到了。这不是一个好模型，而是测量方法的缺陷。

steps.output:
150 units, 500 sensors, 75 failures
control, labels shuffled: mean ROC AUC 0.818 over 5 shuffles

title.en: Find which step leaks
title.zh: 找出是哪一步在泄漏

body.en:
`compare.py` isolates each step. Four rows, all with the same data, model and folds: the scaler fitted on all rows first; the selector fitted on all rows first; both fitted first (what `train.py` does); and both inside a `Pipeline`. A `Pipeline` chains steps into one estimator, and `cross_val_score` refits the whole chain on the training part of each fold only, so the held-out fold never influences a fitted step.

Read down the column. The selector row jumps. The scaler row matches the Pipeline to three decimals in this run. `StandardScaler` uses only feature means and spreads, never the labels, so its leak does not show here, but it is the same mistake and it can show on other data. `SelectKBest(f_classif)` chooses the 10 columns most related to the labels. With 500 columns and 150 rows, some noise columns will correlate with the labels by chance, and a selector that has seen every label picks them; the held-out rows then look predictable because the labels helped choose the columns.

Both leaks are the same mistake: a fitted step saw the held-out rows. One of them is cheap to commit and costly to discover.
body.zh:
`compare.py` 把每一步单独隔离出来。四行，数据、模型和折划分全部相同：先用全部行拟合缩放器；先用全部行拟合选择器；两者都先拟合（`train.py` 的做法）；两者都放在 `Pipeline` 里。`Pipeline` 把多个步骤串成一个估计器，`cross_val_score` 只在每一折的训练部分上重新拟合整条链，因此留出的那一折永远不会影响任何拟合的步骤。

顺着这一列读下来。选择器那一行大幅上跳。这次运行里，缩放器那一行和 Pipeline 在三位小数内相同。`StandardScaler` 只用特征的均值和离散程度，从不看标签，所以它的泄漏在这里看不出来，但错误的性质相同，换一份数据就可能显现。`SelectKBest(f_classif)` 选出与标签最相关的 10 列。500 列配 150 行时，总有一些噪声列碰巧与标签相关，看过全部标签的选择器会选中它们；留出的行于是看起来可预测，其实是标签参与了选列。

两种泄漏是同一个错误：某个已拟合的步骤看到了留出的行。其中一种犯起来代价小，发现起来代价大。

variant                                   ROC AUC
scaler fitted on all rows, then CV          0.676
selector fitted on all rows, then CV        0.824
both fitted on all rows, then CV            0.825
both inside a Pipeline                      0.676

title.en: The same four variants with no signal at all
title.zh: 同样四种做法，但完全没有信号

body.en:
Shuffle the labels and run all four again, averaged over five shuffles. The truth is chance, around 0.5, for every row. A row that is far above it is not measuring the sensors. It is measuring how much the procedure lets the answer into the question.

This is the check to add to any evaluation script you did not write: a shuffled-label control costs one extra run and catches a whole class of mistakes.
body.zh:
打乱标签，把四种做法再各跑一遍，取五次打乱的平均。此时对每一行来说真相都是随机水平，约 0.5。哪一行远高于它，它测的就不是传感器，而是这套流程让答案泄漏进问题的程度。

对任何不是你写的评估脚本，都应加上这项检查：打乱标签的对照只多花一次运行，却能抓住一整类错误。

title.en: What happens in production
title.zh: 上线之后会怎样

body.en:
`--fresh` draws a new batch of 3,000 units from the same simulated plant, which the model has never seen, trains the final model on the original 150, and scores the new units. Compare three lines: the estimate from the leaky procedure, the honest estimate from the Pipeline, and the score on the new batch.

Notice what did not change. The model that gets deployed is identical under both procedures, because both finally fit on all 150 units. Leakage did not make the model worse. It made the number you used to decide worse. Jack committed the rig on the leaky number and got what the Pipeline row had said all along. A team that then tunes `k` or compares models with the leaky number will also choose the wrong settings, because each choice is rewarded for fitting the held-out rows.

In real life you rarely have 3,000 new labelled units to check against. That is why the Pipeline and the shuffled-label control matter: they are the cheap way to get the honest figure before deployment.
body.zh:
`--fresh` 从同一个模拟工厂再生成一批 3,000 个模型从未见过的单元，用原来的 150 个训练最终模型，再给这批新单元打分。比较三行：带泄漏的流程给出的估计、Pipeline 给出的诚实估计，以及在新批次上的得分。

注意没有变的东西。两种流程部署出去的模型是完全相同的，因为它们最终都在全部 150 个单元上拟合。泄漏没有让模型变差，它让你据以决策的那个数字变差了。Jack 按带泄漏的数字下了注，得到的却是 Pipeline 那一行从头到尾说的水平。接着用泄漏的数字去调 `k` 或比较模型的团队，也会选错设置，因为每一次选择都因“更贴合留出的行”而得到奖励。

现实中你很少有 3,000 个新的带标签单元可供核对。所以 Pipeline 和打乱标签的对照才重要：它们是在部署之前得到诚实数字的廉价办法。
